label: Gatterer visual/material evidentiary systems are established prior art

observations.value: Gatterer's historical knowledge was shaped by verbal, visual and material media; engraved plates participated in evidentiary authority, collaborative production and reproduction error.

sources.citation: André de Melo Araújo, Evidentiary Authority as a System, Berichte zur Wissenschaftsgeschichte 48.3 (2025): 203-226

claim_limit: Demotes generic visual-evidence/media claims; does not address the full longitudinal Nürnberg host/plate ecology reconstructed here.

label: Long-duration frontispiece prototype/reuse studies are established prior art

observations.value: Systematic eighteenth-century frontispiece census can identify multiple prototypes and follow reuse/variation across editions, abridgments and chapbooks while tracking reinterpretation by booksellers, engravers and readers.

sources.citation: Russell Palmer, Robinson Crusoe Portrait Frontispieces: Models, Variants, and Interpretations, 1719-1799, PBSA 119.1 (2025): 39-98

claim_limit: Demotes novelty claims based only on century-scale prototype genealogy or changed host meaning.

label: Reused designs acquire context-dependent meanings across media

sources.citation: Sandro Jung, Eighteenth-Century Illustration and Literary Material Culture: Richardson, Thomson, Defoe (Cambridge, 2023)

observations.value: Reuse/redaction of designs across new media and host contexts can alter relational meaning without requiring physical plate identity.

label: Antiquarian copperplate production/circulation as media ecology is established prior art

sources.citation: Noah Heringman and Crystal B. Lake, Antiquarian Media Ecologies in the Eighteenth Century, Modern Philology 120.1 (2022): 1-23

observations.value: Antiquarian copperplate engravings circulated within visual/verbal networks including objects, manuscript debate, sketches and preparatory drawings.

label: Physical printing-plate provenance, custody, repair and reprinting are established research objects

sources.citation: Chiara Betti, Lost Treasures Resurface: The Untold Story of the Society of Antiquaries' Printing Plates, Antiquaries Journal 104 (2024): 304-342

observations.value: Historical copperplates can be studied as surviving objects with provenance, post-engraver custody, widow/heir publication, repair, alterations, renewed printing and state/paper comparison.

claim_limit: Strongly validates matrix/state ontology but removes ontology or plate afterlife itself as a novelty claim.

label: Archive-backed longitudinal history of one copperplate is established prior art

sources.citation: Karen L. Bowen and Dirk Imhof, 18,257 Impressions from a Plate, Print Quarterly 22.3 (2005): 265-279
Karen L. Bowen and Dirk Imhof, Christopher Plantin and Engraved Book Illustrations in Sixteenth-Century Europe (Cambridge, 2008)

observations.value: A title plate can be followed over decades through archival payments, physical reworkings/states, impression counts, production economics and plate-stock inventories.

claim_limit: Sets a high evidentiary standard for same-matrix claims; the Nürnberg archive may not permit equivalent quantitative reconstruction.

label: Reader-driven extra-illustration and copy remaking are established prior art

sources.citation: Lucy Peltz, Facing the Text: Extra-Illustration, Print Culture, and Society in Britain, 1769-1840 (Huntington Library Press, 2017)
Multigraph Collective, Thickening, in Interacting with Print (Chicago, 2018), pp. 288-304

observations.value: Owners/readers can remake published books by tipping or pasting visual/printed material into copies, producing interpretive and self-reflexive composite artifacts.

claim_limit: The present contribution lies in connecting private augmentation to an already modular serial armorial apparatus, not in discovering extra-illustration.

label: Göttingen institutionalisation of material evidence and historical sciences is established prior art

sources.citation: Peter N. Miller, Material Evidence in the History Curriculum in Eighteenth-Century Göttingen, in History and Its Objects (Cornell, 2017), pp. 76-96
Martin Gierl, Geschichte als präzisierte Wissenschaft: Johann Christoph Gatterer und die Historiographie des 18. Jahrhunderts im ganzen Umfang (2012)

observations.value: Göttingen systematised material evidence, auxiliary historical sciences and a professional/institutional programme of historical method.

claim_limit: The project should ask how an older Nürnberg publication infrastructure was selectively rehosted/re-specified within this programme, not claim that Göttingen invented material evidence.

label: Defensible gap: Nürnberg serial apparatus to Göttingen re-specification

observations.value: Existing scholarship located in the final sweep does not directly reconstruct the Historia/Genealogia/Heraldica programme and related Nürnberg armorial/genealogical plate apparatus across programme/design/matrix/state/witness/copy levels and then ask how that pre-existing serial/recombinable infrastructure was selectively rehosted and epistemically re-specified in the Gatterer/Göttingen historical-science environment.

claim_limit: A negative historiographical claim is bounded by the search performed. Reopen if a directly overlapping Weigel/Köhler/Gatterer/Raspe or Historia Genealogia Heraldica study is identified.
